words.meaning: to silence a microphone, speaker, or chat notifications
words.example: Please mute your microphone when you are not speaking in the meeting.

words.meaning: a trial period at the start of a new job
words.example: During the six-month probation, the manager checks your work closely.

words.meaning: a short period of work experience to learn a job
words.example: My sister got a summer internship at a design company.

words.meaning: unwanted messages or emails sent to many people at once
words.example: I get so much spam in my inbox that I miss important emails.

words.meaning: a person with a large online audience who can change what people buy or think
words.example: The influencer recommended a new skincare brand to her two million followers.

words.meaning: a small item, like a scarf or a necklace, that completes an outfit

words.example: These cookies are soft in the middle and slightly chewy.

grammar.title: Non-Defining Relative Clauses
grammar.explanation:
We use **non-defining relative clauses** to add extra information about a noun. The sentence still makes sense without the extra part.

My sister, who lives in Toronto, works as a tailor. Remove **who lives in Toronto**, and the sentence is still complete.

Use **who** for people, **which** for things, and **whose** for possession. An influencer, who has two million followers, visited our office.

Always put **commas** around a non-defining clause. Without commas, the clause is necessary information, not extra.

Never use **that** in a non-defining clause. Say *the bonus, which was generous* — not *the bonus, that was generous*.
examples: *The intern, *who* passed her probation, got a full-time offer.* (who + commas = extra info about a person)
*My networking contacts, *who* work in finance, sent me job tips.* (who for people)
*Her bonus, *which* arrived in December, paid for a holiday.* (which + commas = extra info about a thing)
*The spam email, *which* looked real, was actually a scam.* (which for things)
*The influencer, *whose* followers trust her, recommended the accessory.* (whose = possession)
*His decision to resign, *which* surprised everyone, was the right move.* (which can refer to a whole idea)

practice.q: Complete: My sister, ___ lives in Paris, is a tailor. (who / that)
practice.a: Who. Say: My sister, who lives in Paris, is a tailor.

practice.q: Complete: The cookies, ___ were slightly chewy, disappeared fast. (which / that)
practice.a: Which. Say: The cookies, which were slightly chewy, disappeared fast.

practice.q: Complete: The manager, ___ team passed probation, paid a bonus. (whose / who)
practice.a: Whose. Say: The manager, whose team passed probation, paid a bonus.

practice.q: Complete: His internship, ___ started in June, taught him a lot. (which / who)
practice.a: Which. Say: His internship, which started in June, taught him a lot.
